solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Husband's crazy for hottie — will his wife do this?

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for husband, as in genealogies

indicators.note: crazy says the letters of the following words are jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A husband goes wild over an attractive woman, and the clue asks how his wife will react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' scrambles FOR HOTTIE into ITTHEROOF, which follows H.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for flying into a furious rage, just what a betrayed spouse might do.

clue.text: Blowing top, hit journalist

indicators.note: blowing one's top here means losing the top letter of the word for hit

parts.note: to whack someone is to hit them

explanation.surface: Someone loses their temper and strikes a reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blowing top' looks like losing one's temper; it drops the first letter, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Hack is an informal, often disparaging word for a jobbing writer or reporter.

clue.text: Seventeen soprano works without introduction from Vaughan Williams?

indicators.note: works suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for soprano in vocal scores

indicators.note: introduction from takes just the opening letter of the following name

explanation.surface: A musical piece for seventeen sopranos composed by Ralph Vaughan Williams, the English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: SEVENTEEN plus S, 'without' V (the opening of Vaughan), is rearranged ('works'). The definition needs a different Williams: the playwright Tennessee Williams.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee Williams was the American playwright, so this Williams is one example, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Hospital on island raised capital

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above the following piece

parts.note: H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is written upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A hospital built on an island was elevated to capital status.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a small Hebridean island off Scotland; in a down entry the hospital sits on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hanoi is the capital city of Vietnam, a straightforward example.

clue.text: Intolerant sort swallows pill to become most spirited

indicators.note: swallows means one piece takes the other inside itself

parts.note: a racist is a person intolerant of other races
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A bigot takes a pill to liven up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallows' puts E (ecstasy) inside RACIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Racy means lively or risqué, so the superlative fits the most lively.

clue.text: Rocky Marciano initially abandoned wind instrument

indicators.note: rocky means unsteady or shaky, so the letters are shaken into a new order
initially abandoned means the boxer's surname loses its first letter

explanation.surface: Boxer Rocky Marciano at first gave up a wind instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' is the boxer's first name on the surface; it is the anagram signal for ARCIANO, which is MARCIANO without its M.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocarina is a small, egg-shaped flute played by blowing, so it is a woodwind.

clue.text: Contribution to speech therapy is genuine

indicators.note: Contribution to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that some input to speech therapy is the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Echt is a German loanword in English for authentic or real, and 'is' joins the adjective as a predicate.

clue.text: Cold meat that's soft to chew

parts.note: C is the cold tap abbreviation
ham is a cured meat
p (piano) is the musical marking for soft

explanation.surface: Cold meat that is tender enough to eat easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft' looks like a description of the meat; it is P, the musical direction piano.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or bite noisily, as a horse champs at the bit.

clue.text: What decides winner of cup after match? That's about right

indicators.note: after puts the cup piece behind the match piece

parts.note: a tie is a match between teams, as in a cup tie

indicators.note: That's about says the cup goes around the following letter

parts.note: a beaker is a drinking cup

explanation.surface: A sports question about settling a cup match, with a reply that this is about right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's about right' reads as agreement but means the cup goes round R.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreaker is an extra game or question used to separate level contestants.

clue.text: Boozy event at university reflected by fighting outside clubs

indicators.note: reflected means turned back, so the word reads in reverse

parts.note: up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

indicators.note: outside means the fighting word wraps round the clubs letter

parts.note: a brawl is a fight
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A drinking session at college is mirrored by brawling outside nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflected' turns UP into PU; BRAWL goes 'outside' C to make BCRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub crawl is a drinking tour of several pubs in one outing.

clue.text: Cleric provides a series of prayers

definitions.meaning: a clergyman attached to a cathedral chapter
the fixed central part of the Mass, the eucharistic prayer

explanation.surface: A clergyman supplies a sequence of prayers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a cathedral clergyman and the unchanging prayer of the Mass.

clue.text: Set in stone, union laws originally started by firm

indicators.note: started by puts the firm abbreviation at the front

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: in puts those opening letters inside the stone

parts.note: agate is a banded semi-precious stone

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letters of the two following words

explanation.surface: Union rules carved in stone, first introduced by a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set in stone' looks like one idiom; 'Set' alone is the definition, and 'in stone' starts the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To set is to thicken or clot, as blood or jelly does.

clue.text: Disease that's transmitted orally put one in grave situation twice

indicators.note: twice asks for the sounded word two times over
transmitted orally means spoken, so we want what the words sound like

parts.note: to bury someone is to put them in a grave

explanation.surface: A disease spread by mouth that puts a person in a grave condition twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transmitted orally' reads like infection by mouth; it signals sound. BURY BURY said aloud gives the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Beriberi is a deficiency illness caused by lack of vitamin B1.

clue.text: After Kelvin's gone back once more fill skip

indicators.note: back means the remaining letters are read in reverse
gone means the kelvin letter is removed

parts.note: to repack is to fill again
K is the symbol for the kelvin temperature unit

explanation.surface: Once Kelvin has returned, the skip is filled again.
explanation.walkthrough: REPACK without K is REPAC, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful leap, so to caper is to skip about.

clue.text: Beer that's drunk by motorist ultimately shown in this?

definitions.text: Beer that's drunk by motorist ultimately shown in this?

indicators.note: drunk says the letters are muddled up
ultimately takes the final letter of the word before

explanation.surface: Beer a driver drank would be revealed by this roadside test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' scrambles BEER THAT'S into BREATHTES, then T ends motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A breathalyser check reveals alcohol consumed by a driver.

clue.text: Secret police at first resolved to show consideration

indicators.note: resolved means broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged
at first takes the opening letter of police

explanation.surface: The secret police first made up their minds to be considerate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges SECRET plus P.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard someone with esteem is to show them consideration.

clue.text: European vote's inclined to be prolonged

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper
tended means was inclined to

explanation.surface: A European vote tends to drag on.
explanation.definitionFit: Lengthened in time is the sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Type of book that will be returned undamaged?

indicators.note: the whole entry read backwards comes out unchanged

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A library book that will come back in good condition.
explanation.walkthrough: An Aga saga is a British genre of novel set among the comfortable rural middle class, named after the Aga range cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: A light domestic fiction genre, so it names a kind of novel.

clue.text: Knack one needs to suppress plant

parts.note: art is skill or knack
I is the Roman numeral one
to choke is to stifle or suppress

explanation.surface: A skill someone needs to hold back a growing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is a thistle-like vegetable plant.

clue.text: One who incites abstainer to crack a drink

indicators.note: to crack means to break into, so the abstainer goes inside

parts.note: beer is a drink
TT means teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: An agitator who gets a teetotaller to give in and take a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to crack' reads as giving in, but it means breaking into the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to encourage wrongdoing, so this is an encourager or accomplice.

clue.text: Reportedly violent fellow?

parts.note: said aloud, the word is like rough 'un, a rough one

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a thug, and the word itself sounds like 'rough 'un'.
explanation.definitionFit: A thug or brute is someone known for violence.

clue.text: French writer suffered, hiding in shelter

indicators.note: hiding in means the second word goes inside the shelter

parts.note: a cote is a shelter for doves or sheep
let means allowed, an old sense of suffered

explanation.surface: A French author who endured hardship while concealed in a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffered' means allowed (as in 'suffer the little children'), not endured.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette was the French novelist who wrote Gigi.

clue.text: Is youngster able to find place to eat?

parts.note: can means is able to
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A question whether a youngster can find somewhere to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A canteen is a cafeteria at a workplace or school.

clue.text: One bird or another seen around river with duck

indicators.note: around means the hen wraps round the other letters

parts.note: another bird here is a hen
R is the map abbreviation for river
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots one bird or another near a river with a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not a bird here but nought, O.
explanation.definitionFit: The grey heron is a large wading bird.

clue.text: Cathedral city's epitaph for cricket side?

parts.note: RIP, rest in peace, is a common gravestone inscription
the on side is the leg side of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A city's tribute to a dead cricket team.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a small cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon in Yorkshire has a cathedral and city status.

clue.text: Extremists are jerks with freak as leader

indicators.note: as leader puts the enthusiast piece first

parts.note: a freak is an enthusiast, as in a film freak, so a fan
A is the abbreviation for the are, a unit of area
tics are involuntary jerks

explanation.surface: Extremists are idiots led by a weirdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerks' and 'freak' look like insults; they are twitches and an enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Zealots with extreme beliefs are commonly called by this name.

clue.text: Old queen's wearing extremely terrible hat

indicators.note: wearing means the outer letters are worn around the others
extremely takes the outermost letters of terrible

parts.note: QU is an abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An old queen is wearing a truly awful hat.
explanation.walkthrough: T and E go round O and QU.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, also the chef's tall white cap.

clue.text: Saucy material turns up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the word reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric

explanation.surface: Racy fabric appears punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' looks like arrives; in a down entry it means read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheeky or impudent behaviour is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Its characters often become stars

parts.note: a swear word in print often has its letters replaced by asterisks

explanation.walkthrough: 'characters' and 'stars' suggest actors becoming famous; they are letters and asterisks.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath or swear word is often printed with asterisks to hide it.

clue.text: Refer to question Goethe oddly dismissed

indicators.note: oddly dismissed means the odd-placed letters are dropped and the even ones kept

explanation.surface: A query referring to Goethe was strangely rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping G, E, H from GOETHE leaves OTE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cite a passage is to mention or refer to it.

clue.text: Fish and cask ale for starter

parts.note: a tun is a large cask

indicators.note: for starter takes the opening letter of ale

explanation.surface: A menu: fish, with cask ale to start.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuna is a large sea fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Whatever happens, heartless nurse still stops it

indicators.note: stops means the pieces plug the gap inside the last word
heartless means the central letter is removed

parts.note: a nanny is a children's nurse
even can mean still, as in even more

explanation.surface: No matter what, a callous nurse still puts a halt to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle N from NANNY, leaving NANY; with EVEN it 'stops' (fills) IT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning regardless or come what may.
